PullRequest.Title: agent host: refactor: adopt experimental AHP canvas channels

## Summary

Migrates the local Copilot canvas support already on `main` from its temporary VS Code-specific transport to the experimental canvas channel merged in [microsoft/agent-host-protocol#472](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/472).

- keeps stable chat state limited to minimal canvas resource references
- publishes full live presentation state, including the optional HTTP(S) source, on independently subscribable `ahp-canvas:` channels
- removes the private `vscode/canvases/v1` notification, source-resolution request, initialize capability, and parallel snapshot model
- preserves the existing `chat.agentHost.canvases.enabled` runtime/presentation gate and durable local-Copilot-only product policy
- keeps shared Sessions state provider-neutral

The synced AHP source is pinned to the merged PR commit `6eec1b91`.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Runtime["Copilot runtime canvas events"]
    Projection["CopilotAgentSession projection"]
    Chat["ChatState.canvases references"]
    Canvas["Experimental CanvasState channel"]
    Client["AHP resource subscription"]
    Sessions["Provider-neutral ISessionCanvas"]
    Editor["Existing Sessions canvas editor"]

    Runtime --> Projection
    Projection -->|membership only| Chat
    Projection -->|metadata + optional URL| Canvas
    Chat --> Client
    Canvas --> Client
    Client --> Sessions
    Sessions --> Editor
```

### Host projection and lifecycle

A true canvas-open event creates a new lifetime-scoped `ahp-canvas:` resource. Metadata or source changes retain that resource and emit `canvas/stateChanged`; provider unavailability clears the source through full-state replacement. Closing the canvas removes chat membership and prunes the channel. Session/chat teardown also clears owned channels.

Canvas subscriptions are live-only. They return existing host state, pin the owning session through the normal subscription residency path, and never restore a provider or replay an open/action request. The existing eight-canvas bound and restart non-restoration behavior remain unchanged.

### Client and Sessions adaptation

The protocol client uses the standard subscription manager and canonical canvas reducer, preserving exact host-advertised resource URIs rather than reconstructing remote identities.

The Agent Host Sessions provider follows each advertised canvas reference with a cached resource-scoped subscription and projects immutable provider-neutral state. Unknown membership is distinct from an authoritative empty collection, and pending/error channel state retains membership without a live source.

Presentation support remains a local provider decision: durable local Copilot sessions expose `supportsCanvases`; remote, Claude, and Codex sessions do not. The existing setting and AI entitlement still control actual runtime enablement and editor presentation.

### Privacy and stale-load protection

Canvas URLs are redacted from AHP action, snapshot, initialize/reconnect, and replay diagnostics without mutating live state. Sources remain HTTP(S)-only. The editor keeps local input, source, owner, and load-sequence checks and disposes superseded BrowserViews. Metadata/source changes do not reopen a user-dismissed canvas.

## Removed temporary surfaces

- `AgentCanvasAvailability`, `IAgentCanvas`, and `IAgentCanvasSnapshot`
- `IAgentHostCanvases` and `IAgentService.onDidChangeCanvases`
- `vscode/canvases/v1/changed` and `vscode/canvases/v1/resolveSource`
- the VS Code-specific canvas initialize capability and metadata helpers
- revision-fenced source resolution

A separate AHP agent capability is intentionally absent: clients cannot initiate canvas operations in this scope, and server-published chat references are sufficient discovery. A capability can be introduced later alongside client-originated open/action operations if needed.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed
- focused Agent Host, Sessions provider, canvas service, and layout unit tests — 30 passed
- bundled Copilot runtime/provider integration — 1 passed
- strict Copilot prompt replay — 24 passed
- changed-file ESLint — passed for 35 files
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed
- pre-commit hygiene — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

## Explicitly deferred

- canvas-first or zero-turn chats
- manual canvas picker
- UI-originated canvas open/action requests
- restoration across VS Code/runtime restart
- remote Agent Host, Claude, or Codex presentation
- built-in Office, browser, or terminal canvas providers

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed test proves the before/after payload, and the turn-action-to-summary-to-broadcast call path is explicit. Only the typical chat/client counts and exact duration are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: serialized chat-summary objects and IPC bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(C * K) payload processing per start/completion, where C is the non-tool chat count and K is connected clients; the 100 ms scheduler only coalesces transitions within one window.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased IPC traffic and CPU/GC pressure on turn transitions
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Per-chat status was omitted from the compact root catalog, so turn activity changed only scalar session fields and did not attach `changes.chats`.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A single chat's InProgress/Idle transition now changes the projected compact-chat array, so the notifier sends the entire array and the protocol server broadcasts it to every active client.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 514 copies each chat's volatile status into the compact root catalog. The changed protocol-server test now expects a complete `changes.chats` array after `ChatTurnStarted`; before the diff it expected only scalar `modifiedAt` and `status`.
Findings.Title: Avoid replacing the full chat catalog on turn status changes
Findings.Impact: Each normal turn generally sends a full chat catalog at start and completion. Sessions with many peer/side chats incur extra IPC serialization, parsing, allocation, and GC even though only one chat changed.
Findings.Evidence: `_onChatStateChanged` updates chat status and marks the summary dirty. `SessionSummaryNotifier.flush` assigns all of `current.chats` whenever one projected entry differs. `_broadcastNotification` sends root notifications to every active client without subscription filtering.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep volatile activity bits off the full-replacement root catalog until a single-chat delta is available, or introduce a compact per-chat status delta and reserve full replacement for membership/reordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, update, dismiss, and close a live Copilot canvas in the active chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A runtime canvas event publishes state, then chat membership; the client must receive membership and complete one canvas-channel subscription before `SessionCanvasEditor` can create the BrowserView and navigate to the HTTP(S) source. Metadata-only updates with an unchanged source stay off the BrowserView load path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish chat membership and subscribe to the exact canvas resource for its current state; later source changes arrive as canvas actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold subscription request/snapshot per distinct advertised canvas URI, at most eight live canvases per chat; duplicate consumers share the subscription by exact resource. Updates are one action per changed canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A custom full-chat snapshot was broadcast, then presentation issued one source-resolution IPC request. The new subscription request replaces that source-resolution request rather than adding an extra per-load boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial snapshot is required to obtain the source before presentation; subsequent metadata is off the network-navigation path unless the source changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an external BrowserView and navigate to the advertised HTTP(S) canvas source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One navigation per newly presented source; unchanged metadata/status does not reload, and stale concurrent creations are disposed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor already created the same external BrowserView after resolving the source through IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The navigation is the dominant presentation boundary and must complete for canvas content to appear.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct live canvas resources in the active chat, capped at eight after host eviction; exact-resource subscription sharing is the effective cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The subscription manager coalesces consumers of the same resource. Different canvases may subscribe independently, with an aggregate burst bounded by eight; this is comparable to the prior ability to present the eight-item snapshot.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold resources perform one subscribe; warm duplicate consumers reuse the managed subscription. Removal disposes the reference and unsubscribes. Errors remain represented as unavailable membership rather than being retried per render; no persistent negative cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the action, subscription, editor, sharing, and cleanup paths are explicit and covered by changed tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: BrowserView and page-load duration depend on the canvas provider, but those boundaries predate the diff. Canvas update frequency is provider-dependent and bounded in retained cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new per-resource IPC is bounded and coalesced, replaces on-demand source resolution, and does not increase BrowserView/network cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start and complete turns in a session containing multiple peer or side chats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat turn actions update the chat and session summaries; after the 100 ms summary debounce, a root notification is serialized and sent to every connected client before their session/chat list state reflects the transition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast `root/sessionSummaryChanged` containing the complete compact chat catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one notification at turn start and one at completion, each carrying all C non-tool chats to each of K connected clients; transitions inside one 100 ms window coalesce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notification carried scalar session status/modifiedAt only because per-chat status was absent from the compact catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Clients must deserialize and apply the notification to update list status, so payload size directly affects turn-state UI propagation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective collection is the session's default plus user-created peer/side chats after tool-origin chats are filtered out; there is no chat-count cap found in this path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The notifier serializes changes through one 100 ms scheduler, but the protocol server fans each resulting notification out to all active clients without subscription filtering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Projected arrays are weakly cached by the session chat-array identity, but each status update creates a new array. The cache does not prevent the full payload from being compared, serialized, and sent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the updated test explicitly asserts the newly added full `chats` payload after `ChatTurnStarted`, and the broadcast path is direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most sessions have few chats and clients, so exact byte and latency impact varies; long-lived multi-chat sessions provide a realistic scaling trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: volatile activity status turns scalar turn notifications into O(C * K) full-catalog serialization and IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconnect, remove canvas membership, or tear down its owning chat/session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A reconnect subscribes to each currently observed advertised resource; membership removal disposes client references, and chat/session invalidation prunes host canvas state. Cleanup is not on the BrowserView navigation path except when closing removed inputs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect/subscribe snapshots and unsubscribe removed canvas channels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation per distinct retained canvas resource, bounded at eight per chat and shared per exact URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The custom transport replayed current full-chat snapshots on reconnect and sent explicit empty snapshots for removals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reconnect needs snapshots before live canvas presentation resumes; cleanup does not block unrelated chat progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Currently advertised resources only; removed resources are pruned from the host map and subscription cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent resource subscriptions can proceed concurrently, bounded by the live canvas cap; session residency coordinates release and prevents restore races.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm managed subscriptions are shared. Removed membership releases subscriptions and host state; session/chat teardown clears all owned channels. Missing resources return NotFound rather than restoring providers or repeatedly probing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cleanup and subscription ownership are explicit in state-manager, provider, and subscription-manager tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reconnect prevalence and number of simultaneous canvases vary, but the hard cap bounds the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: lifecycle cleanup is complete and reconnect work remains bounded by the same eight-canvas policy.

Scenarios.Scenario: Write AHP diagnostic JSONL containing canvas actions and snapshots
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Messages are serialized with the redacting replacer and queued into the existing batched file drain; logging is diagnostic and not required for canvas presentation progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Traverse JSON values and clone only canvas action/snapshot wrappers whose state contains a URL, replacing the URL before stringify.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per logged value traversal; canvas wrapper cloning occurs only for matching action/snapshot records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Redaction tracked source-resolution request IDs and cloned matching response objects before stringify.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded CPU/allocation inside diagnostic logging but remains within the existing serialization pass and downstream line limits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append queued JSONL buffers through the logger drain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing batched drain behavior; the diff does not add writes or flushes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same messages used the same batched file queue and size truncation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the canvas critical path through the scheduled pending queue.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Diagnostic message count and payload size, already bounded by logger line/string limits downstream.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single scheduled drain preserves ordering and coalesces pending buffers; no new concurrent filesystem burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Removal of the request-ID set also removes its former bounded retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: serialization and drain placement are visible in the changed logger and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Diagnostic logging enablement and traffic vary, but boundary count is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: redaction moved into the existing stringify traversal without increasing filesystem operations or introducing unbounded retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 56 changed files and all diff pages. One medium IPC/serialization regression was submitted: volatile chat status now forces full compact-chat catalogs into ordinary turn notifications. Canvas channel work is capped, subscription-coalesced, and cleaned up; BrowserView/network and logger filesystem boundary counts are not increased.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
